Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for moving quickly on the MSA and order form. Legal has a couple of asks before we sign the amendment: specifically around the security exhibit — we need clarity on the pen test observation window and exactly what you will provide after the test (logs, sampling manifest, activity timeline).

Two questions to start:
- Can Redwood support an "observation window" where our security team can observe the pen test live (remotely) for up to 2 days?
- What format will the technical handback take? Our audit team needs a clear manifest we can reference (timestamps, sampled sessions, and confirmatory hashes where applicable).

We also need to confirm SOC 2 evidence that will be available to us under the exhibit and whether we can point to a forensic-access process vs. full inspection. Darren and I can share our preferred language but want to see Redwood's baseline first.

Can we get a proposed schedule and a short checklist for the handback items by end of week? We are aiming to finalize the order form this month.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Security, Lumina Health

Subject: Re: Security exhibit + pen test observation window and handback

Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Drafting a short, operational plan below so we can align legal redlines to concrete operations. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that helps.

Proposal (operational):
- Observation: Redwood can provide a remote "observation window" for up to 48 hours. Observers will have a view-only WebRTC stream from the staging environment and an event stream (log tail) with a 5-minute delay to protect ongoing safety tooling.
- Technical handback deliverables (post-test):
  * Sampling manifest (CSV): session id, start/end timestamp, tester identifier, scope flags
  * Aggregated telemetry export (JSONL): relevant system events (no customer PII), retention hashes for sampled files
  * Test timeline PDF: chronological notes and confirmed remediation items
  * Privileged account audit log slice (if forensic access is invoked)
- Timing: deliverables issued within 7 business days after test completion unless we agree to an expedited 48-hour turnaround for critical findings.

From a contracting perspective we recommend:
1) Limit inspection to "forensic access" defined as time-boxed, read-only access to specific logs/snapshots and exclude broad production access.
2) Exclude customer PII from delivered telemetry — we will provide sampled artifacts with redactions/hashes.

I've attached a proposed schedule (pen-test-observation-schedule.csv) and a one-page technical handback checklist (technical-handback-checklist.pdf). Karthik/legal will propose contract language to mirror this operational plan.

Propose next steps:
- Karthik to drop redline for exhibit (order form appendix)
- Call Thursday 4pm PT to confirm window and sign-off

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Stephanie / team — looping in a condensed legal proposal. Inline summary of suggested redline language that maps to the operations Stephanie outlined. Please note I kept the language intentionally narrow to limit long-term obligations.

Suggested contract language (draft):
- "Inspection and Forensic Access": Customer may request forensic access limited to (i) time-boxed read-only snapshots of application logs and system telemetry; (ii) sampled session manifests; and (iii) aggregated, non-PII telemetry exports. Forensic access requests require no less than 48 hours' notice and are limited to two observation windows per 12-month period unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- "Exclusions and Privacy": Redwood will exclude customer personal data and any third-party customer content from delivered artifacts. Where sampling is required, Redwood will supply cryptographic hashes for sampled files and a manifest describing redaction steps.
- "Remediation and Delivery SLA": Redwood will deliver the technical handback package within 7 business days or, for critical/high severity findings, within 48 hours. Delivery constitutes a production of evidence for audit use; it does not constitute acceptance of liability.

Open items for us to confirm with the customer:
1) Is Lumina comfortable with the two-windows-per-year cap?
2) Will Lumina require live interactive queries during observation (we should avoid ad-hoc queries that risk escalated access)?
3) Confirm point of contact for account provisioning for observers (we need full name + corporate email + MFA steps).

I attached a redline draft (Lumina_Security_Exhibit_Redlines_v1.docx). Recommend we send that to Alice with the schedule and a one-paragraph cover note.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Lumina_Security_Exhibit_Redlines_v1.docx
